entry.title: Homothetic Self-Similar Solutions to the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
entry.summary: We investigate homothetic forward self-similar solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations: the solutions $\overline{U}$ for which both $\overline{U}$ and $β\overline{U}$ are self-similar profiles for some nontrivial $β$. Homothetic solutions are, in addition, the only solutions for which a singular limit argument can be used to prove non-uniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions along the lines of the Jia-Šverák program. In three dimensions, and for sufficiently regular initial data, we prove a Liouville theorem that rules out the existence of non-trivial homothetic solutions. In two dimensions, our Liouville theorem reproves a result of Luo and Shvydkoy that the only decaying homothetic solution with continuous angular data is the Oseen vortex. In addition, we prove that the Euler equations linearized around the Oseen vortex are stable in some subspaces of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$, for example in the space of $2$-fold rotationally symmetric functions. On the other hand, we also discover a homothetic solution for which an unstable approximate eigenvalue of the linearized Euler equations exists.
entry.arxiv:comment: 31 pages. This new version includes an announcement of sharp rigidity theorems for homothetic solutions and rigidity theorems for (-1)-homogeneous Euler solutions up to the Onsager threshold, which we prove in subsequent work. Due to this new work, we eliminated the old Section 2. We also performed additional revisions to maximize clarity and correctness of our exposition

entry.title: Non-uniqueness for the Complex Ginzburg-Landau Equation
entry.summary: We show that singularities of the three-dimensional cubic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation developing from smooth initial data can induce non-uniqueness of solutions after the time of blowup. The solutions we study start as backward self-similar solutions, and the source of the non-uniqueness is an unstable eigenvalue of the linearization around the forward self-similar profile generated by the singularity. We establish the existence of this eigenvalue, and hence the non-uniqueness, by a computer-assisted proof for specific values of the parameters in the equation. The work is in part motivated by similarities to conjectured behavior for the Navier-Stokes equation, with which the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation shares several important properties, such as an energy inequality and the scaling symmetry.

entry.title: A Viscous Cascade Construction of Nonunique Leray--Hopf Solutions to the Unforced 3D Navier--Stokes Equations
entry.summary: We construct a nonzero divergence-free initial velocity on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and a continuum of pairwise distinct suitable Leray--Hopf solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on a common time interval. The initial datum is axisymmetric, smooth away from the origin, and belongs to every $L^{\mathfrak q}$ with $1\leq \mathfrak q<3$, but not to $L^3$. All the solutions attain this datum strongly in $L^2$, are smooth at positive times, and satisfy both the global and local energy equalities through time zero. The same family belongs simultaneously to every $L^{\mathfrak p}_tL^{\mathfrak q}_x$ with $1\leq \mathfrak p\leq\infty$, $2\leq \mathfrak q\leq\infty$, and $2/\mathfrak p+3/\mathfrak q>1$. The same solutions also belong to the critical Lorentz space $L^\infty_tL^{3,\infty}_x$. This endpoint is sharp for uniqueness in the Leray--Hopf class within the Lorentz scale. The proof is entirely analytic and uses a cascade through geometrically separated Gaussian swirls. We establish growth for the time-dependent viscous linearization and determine the sign of its complete quadratic stress, including the interaction of the reference velocity with the second variation. The integrated stress generates a controlled perturbation at the next larger spatial scale. At each finite cutoff, a prescribed terminal coordinate selects an initial perturbation whose physical $L^2$ norm tends to zero as the cutoff is removed. Uniform energy, moment, and transfer estimates yield the common strong initial trace while preserving a nonzero observable at a fixed positive time.
